question.text: What will be the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in New Zealand's total electronic card transaction values for October 2026 (Stats NZ, released 12 November 2026)?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in the total value of electronic card transactions (all industries, i.e. including the services and other non-retail categories) for October 2026, as reported in Stats NZ's information release "Electronic card transactions: October 2026", published on 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT and listed at https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/.

The resolving figure is the percentage Stats NZ states in that release for the change in the seasonally adjusted total value of electronic card spending — the figure in the sentence of the form "the total value of electronic card spending, including the two non-retail categories (services and other non-retail), [increased/decreased] from September 2026, up/down $X million (Y percent)". For example, the September 2026 release reported "down $51 million (0.5 percent)", which corresponds to -0.5.

If the October 2026 release does not state a percentage for the total (all industries) series, the question instead resolves to the percentage change between the seasonally adjusted total values for September 2026 and October 2026 published in that release.
question.fine_print: Resolution uses the figures as first published in the release of 12 November 2026; later revisions to seasonally adjusted levels do not change the answer. If that release is delayed, resolution waits until it is published.

research:
Stats NZ does not publish the October 2026 figure until 12 November 2026, and I found no October card-spending data from any source. Nothing settles the question yet. The total series has fallen 0.5% in each of August and September, and pump prices hit record highs in October.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-16: The September 2026 release reported that the seasonally adjusted total value of card spending, including services and other non-retail, fell $51 million (0.5%) from August, to $9.2 billion actual. Within that, retail fell 0.4% ($30m), core retail fell 0.7% ($41m), other non-retail fell 1.1% ($25m) and services fell 1.5% ($5.9m). Fuel rose 2.9% and hospitality fell 2.3%. Total spending for the September quarter was up 0.3% on the June quarter. The Stats NZ page builds its content with scripts, so I could not read it directly; these figures come from Xinhua. [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20261016/6a516876716c4611bf55a9557d2d4e04/c.html), [Stats NZ](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/electronic-card-transactions-september-2026/)
- 2026-09-15: The August 2026 total fell $48 million (0.5%), retail fell 0.9% ($63m) and services rose 1.2%. Actual spending was $9.4 billion across 172 million transactions. [Stats NZ](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/electronic-card-transactions-august-2026/), [Scoop](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/BU2609/S00169/electronic-card-transactions-august-2026.htm)
- Watch out for Trading Economics: it labels the retail series as "total" (for example, September -0.4% and August -0.9%), so its headlines do not match the resolving series. [TE](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/592524)
- I could not find a CSV of the series or any higher-frequency official data.

### 2. Current status
- 2026-11-02: Nothing settles or nearly settles the question. There is no October ECT, Worldline/Cuscal, Westpac or ANZ card data yet. Worldline sold its NZ payments business to Cuscal on 2026-05-29, and I found no monthly releases from Worldline since then. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/29/3303392/0/en/WORLDLINE-New-Zealand-payment-activities-divestment-finalised-Press-release.html)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Centrix reported that annual liquidations rose 18%, with hospitality's liquidation rate 3.3 times the average. About 15,000 borrowers are in hardship, and 10.88% of credit-active consumers are behind on payments, which is lower than a year earlier. [NZ Herald](https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/annual-liquidations-up-18-as-retail-hospitality-closures-surge/NMZAEAMMTZD7NIKPWA7UP4324U/), [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/2306248/15-000-borrowers-struggling-in-hardship-latest-data)
- 2026-10-31: The national average price for 91 petrol was $3.556/L, 95 was $3.745/L and diesel was $3.206/L (Gaspy data via NZ Fuel Watch). [NZ Fuel Watch](https://www.fuelwatch.nz/)
- 2026-10-16: 95 petrol topped $4/L at some Auckland pumps. One report put the 95 average at about $3.80, up 11% in 28 days, with 91 at $3.61. Z said petrol demand fell about 6% over the second and third quarters. [1News](https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/16/fuel-price-tops-4-at-the-pump/)
- 2026-10-05: 91 petrol hit an all-time high above $3.50/L, with Brent crude above US$100. [1News](https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/05/petrol-price-hits-all-time-high-as-average-litre-of-91-tops-350/)
- October 2026: RBNZ credit card billings for September were up 6.9% year on year (seasonally adjusted). Westpac's Retail Spending Pulse put September card spending up 7.7%. ANZ reported seasonally adjusted card spending up 0.5% month on month in September, with hospitality up 1%. These bank series ran stronger than Stats NZ's. [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/new-zealand-credit-card-spending-sep-yy-69-prev-35), [MPA](https://www.mpamag.com/nz/news/general/card-spending-climbs-77-as-fuel-prices-hit-353-a-litre/592608)
- The general election is on Saturday 7 November 2026, so October was the campaign month. Overseas voting opened on 21 October. In Worldline's data for October 2023, spending stayed weak both before and after that election. [Elections NZ](https://www.elections.nz/2026-general-election), [Worldline 2023](https://worldline.com/en-nz/home/top-navigation/media-relations/press-releases/consumer-spending-growth-in-october-was-weak-both-before-and-after-the-election)

### 4. Base rates
Seasonally adjusted month-on-month changes in the total (all industries) series for 2026:

| Month | Change |
|---|---|
| January | -0.7% |
| February | not found |
| March | not found |
| April | -1.6% |
| May | +2.2% |
| June | not confirmed for the total; retail was about -1.4% |
| July | +1.0% (Trading Economics says July was revised down a little, but that likely refers to retail) |
| August | -0.5% |
| September | -0.5% |

- The typical size of a monthly move is about 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points, and the sign has gone both ways.
- Fuel is roughly 5 to 6% of card spending. A 3 to 8% month-on-month rise in fuel prices in October would mechanically add only about 0.2 to 0.4 points to the total.
- Hospitality has fallen for two months in a row (-1.9% in August, -2.3% in September).
- After two declines, a bounce-back is possible, but I found no data on October in particular.
- I could not find the October 2025 seasonally adjusted total change. One secondary source gives October 2025 actual spending as $9.725 billion. [successknocks](https://successknocks.com/new-zealand-card-spending-october-2025/)

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or published economist forecast for the October 2026 Stats NZ total.
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets matches this question. They cover US merchant card spend, RBNZ decisions and the NZ prime minister. Polymarket prices the February 2027 RBNZ decision at 55.5% for a 25bp hike, which points to inflation pressure rather than anything about spending.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Early November: possible October card updates from Westpac (Retail Spending Pulse), ANZ or BNZ. I have not confirmed release dates.
- 2026-11-07: the general election, which falls after October and so does not affect the resolving data.
- 2026-11-12, 10:45am NZDT: the October 2026 ECT release, which resolves the question. It may also revise September.
- The RBNZ credit card series (20 November) and Selected price indexes (17 November) both come out after resolution.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-16: The Stats NZ September 2026 release page loads its content with scripts, so my tools only got the page title. I could not read the release text or its CSV, and the −0.5% total (−$51m) comes from the question background. [Stats NZ](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/electronic-card-transactions-september-2026/)
- 2026-10-16: Xinhua independently confirms the total fell 0.5% in September. [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20261016/6a516876716c4611bf55a9557d2d4e04/c.html)
- 2026-10-16: Trading Economics reports −0.4% for September and −0.9% for August. Industry figures (fuel +2.9%, hospitality −2.3%) match the question, so its headline is most likely the retail series, not the total. September industry changes: consumables +0.3%, motor vehicles +0.6%, durables −0.4%, apparel −2.0%. August: fuel +1.5%, hospitality −1.9%, apparel −2.0%. [TE](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/592524)
- I could not confirm the August 2026 total (all industries) figure. investinglive also gives August retail as −0.9%. [investinglive](https://investinglive.com/news/new-zealand-card-spending-falls-for-second-month-as-food-prices-hold-flat-in-september/)

### 2. Current status
- 2026-11-02: Not settled. No October Stats NZ, Paymark or ANZ card data has been published.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Centrix reports annual business liquidations up 18%. Hospitality's liquidation rate is 3.3 times the all-sector average, and about 15,000 borrowers are in hardship. [NZ Herald](https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/annual-liquidations-up-18-as-retail-hospitality-closures-surge/NMZAEAMMTZD7NIKPWA7UP4324U/), [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/2306248/15-000-borrowers-struggling-in-hardship-latest-data)
- 2026-10-31: NZ Fuel Watch, quoting Gaspy, puts 91 unleaded at about $3.556/L, up 3.6c over 28 days. I did not check this against Gaspy directly. [Fuel Watch](https://www.fuelwatch.nz/)
- 2026-10-28: The RBNZ surprised markets by holding the OCR at 2.75%; a hike had been priced in. ActionForex reports a 4:3 vote, which I saw in only that one source. [Babypips](https://www.babypips.com/analysis/headline-rbnz-rate-statement-shock-breaking-down-surprise-hold-2026-10-28)
- 2026-10-21: RBNZ September credit card billings, seasonally adjusted, were up 6.9% year on year to $4.7b (August was 3.6%, revised). [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/new-zealand-credit-card-spending-sep-yy-69-prev-35)
- 2026-10-16: September petrol prices rose 6.4% and diesel 7.8% from August. Over the year, petrol is up 24.3% and diesel 55.8%. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/10/16/new-zealand-petrol-diesel-prices-rise-in-september)
- 2026-10-16: Retail NZ says households are spending only on necessities as Q4 begins. [Scoop](https://business.scoop.co.nz/2026/10/16/retail-entering-key-last-quarter-under-real-pressure/)
- 2026-10-05: Gaspy's average for 91 unleaded hit $3.505/L, above the April peak. The NZD was down about 7% since August, to about 55.8 US cents, and Brent was above US$100. [NewsWire](https://newswire.co.nz/2026/10/new-zealand-retail-spending-september-2026-paymark/)
- 2026-10-05: Paymark's September core retail was $3.57b, down 1.3% year on year (August was down 1.8%). Non-food retail fell 7.1% year on year in the last week of September, and fuel spending was up 35% year on year. [NewsWire](https://newswire.co.nz/2026/10/new-zealand-retail-spending-september-2026-paymark/)
- ANZ's September card spending index rose 0.5% month on month, seasonally adjusted. This disagrees with Stats NZ's fall, but the two measures are not directly comparable. [ANZ](https://www.anz.co.nz/about-us/economic-markets-research/merchant-card-spending/)

### 4. Base rates
- 2026 total series (from the question): January −0.7, April −1.6, May +2.2, July +1.0, September −0.5. August is probably about −0.9, but that figure is retail and unconfirmed for the total.
- Over the last three months the total series looks like +1.0, then roughly −0.9, then −0.5. That means two straight falls, with fuel the only consistent riser.
- 2025-10: Trading Economics says October 2025 rose 0.2% month on month, seasonally adjusted, but I did not check whether that is the total or the retail series. [TE](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/501505)
- Typical monthly moves are within about ±1%, with occasional ±1.5 to 2% swings. Rising fuel prices in October (roughly +1 to 3% at the pump) would add a little to nominal values.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or consensus forecast for this release. The Kalshi and Polymarket markets supplied are about US merchant card spend, RBNZ rate decisions and NZ politics, so none of them match this question.
- Economists' previews usually come out only a day or two before release, and I found none yet.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 3 to 6 November (my estimate from past timing): Paymark (now owned by Cuscal) October retail data. It is usually the first look at October spending.
- Early November: ANZ's October card spending note. The page still shows September.
- 12 November, 10:45am NZDT: the resolving Stats NZ release. On 17 November Stats NZ publishes October food and fuel prices, and on 20 November the RBNZ publishes credit card data; both come after resolution.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. Stats NZ releases the October 2026 figure on 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT.

(b) The latest known value is -0.5% for September 2026, released 16 October 2026. August 2026 was also -0.5%.

(c) If nothing changed, a flat month would give 0.0%.

(d) If the trend continued, a third mild decline would give about -0.5%.

(e) Over 2026, the monthly seasonally adjusted change in the total series ranged from -1.6% to +2.2%. The typical absolute move is 0.5 to 1.5 points, so a standard deviation of about 0.9 to 1.0 points is reasonable.

(f) There are no economist or market forecasts. Partial indicators push in different directions:
- **Fuel:** 91 petrol rose roughly 5 to 10% during October to record highs. Fuel is about 5 to 6% of card spending, so this mechanically adds about 0.3 to 0.5 points to the total.
- **Mean reversion:** after two declines in a row, a modest rebound is somewhat more likely.
- **Drags:** the election campaign, weak hospitality and rising liquidations all point lower.
- **Bank data:** ANZ and Westpac card data for September were firmer than Stats NZ's figures.

Overall I put the median slightly positive, at about +0.2%.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low:** fuel price shock demand destruction spreads to hospitality and retail, election uncertainty freezes discretionary spending and September is revised up, giving about -1.5% to -2%.
- **High:** a strong rebound after two weak months combines with record fuel prices and a Labour Day weekend boost not fully removed by seasonal adjustment, giving +1.5% to +2.5%.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. The October 2026 release is due 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT, around 22:00 UTC on 12 November.

(b) **Latest known value:** September 2026, published 16 October 2026: the seasonally adjusted total fell 0.5% ($51 million). August 2026 also fell 0.5%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** A flat month would give about 0.0%. Repeating the last print would give -0.5%.

(d) **If the trend continued:** Two consecutive -0.5% months would point to roughly -0.5% again. However, 2026 shows no persistent trend, and moves of both signs are common.

(e) **Historical variation:** Monthly moves in 2026 ran from -1.6% to +2.2%. The typical absolute move is about 0.5 to 1.5 points, which implies a standard deviation of roughly 1 point.

(f) **Expectations of experts and markets:** No market or economist forecast covers this series. The partial indicators point in different directions:
- **Fuel:** Pump prices rose sharply through October, with 91 petrol reaching record highs and the 95 average up about 11% in 28 days to mid-month. Fuel is about 5 to 6% of spending, so this mechanically adds roughly +0.2 to +0.4 points, partly offset by lower volumes.
- **Bank card data:** ANZ and Westpac card data ran stronger than Stats NZ in September.
- **Drags:** Hospitality is weak and liquidations are rising. October was the election campaign month, and in Worldline's data for October 2023, spending stayed weak around that election.
- **Mean reversion:** After two declines, a small bounce is possible.

On balance I put the median slightly positive, around +0.2%.
